tools.name: 3DCT
tools.approach: Affine 3D-to-2D coordinate transform with fiducial-based least-squares fit to map fluorescence z-stacks onto SEM/FIB images for site-specific cryo-FIB milling.
tools.when_to_use: Standard correlation tool for cryo-FIB site-specific milling guided by FLM z-stacks; widely used with SerialFIB and within METEOR workflows.
tools.limitations: Manual fiducial selection; accuracy limited by FLM PSF and fiducial visibility; classical only.
tools.verification_notes: Arnold, Mahamid, Lucic et al. Biophys. J. 110(4):860-869 (2016). py3DCT/v3 ports by Fung 2021.

tools.name: CLEMSite
tools.approach: Software pipeline for automated phenotypic CLEM screens with FIB-SEM. CLEMSite-LM module identifies fluorescent targets on the grid, CLEMSite-EM Navigator + Multisite re-locates them in the SEM and triggers sequential FIB-SEM volume runs; a Run Checker module supervises long unattended jobs.
tools.architecture: Combines classical image registration with a CNN-based grid-square/landmark detection module.
tools.training_data: EMBL Carl-Zeiss-grid LM/SEM image pairs (in-house annotations).
tools.when_to_use: Room-temperature volume CLEM screens where many cells must be re-found in FIB-SEM without operator intervention; useful when adapting CLEM to medium-throughput discovery workflows.
tools.limitations: Optimised for Zeiss FIB-SEM (Crossbeam) and finder grids similar to those used at EMBL; cryo-CLEM workflows need adaptation; limited tested cells of biological diversity.
tools.compute: Microscope control workstation + 1 GPU for CNN inference.
tools.verification_notes: Serra Lleti JM, Steyer AM, Schieber NL et al., J Cell Biol 222(3):e202209127 (2023). PMID 36562752, DOI 10.1083/jcb.202209127. Russell/Schorb were not first authors as the gap entry suggested; first author is Serra Lleti, corresponding senior author Yannick Schwab.

tools.name: CorRelator
tools.approach: Interactive pixel-to-stage-coordinate transformation with live and post-acquisition correlation between cryo-FLM and TEM/ET; provides real-time positioning during data collection.
tools.when_to_use: Live correlative acquisition on non-integrated systems (standalone FLM + TEM) where 3DCT is insufficient for stage-driven retargeting.
tools.limitations: Designed for cryo-EM/ET only; not for FIB milling; 2D-centric correlation.
tools.verification_notes: Yang, Larson, Sibert, Shrum, Wright. JSB 213(2):107709 (2021).

tools.name: DeepCLEM
tools.approach: CNN predicts in-silico fluorescent chromatin signal from EM micrographs; predicted images are correlated to experimental FLM signal to drive automatic CLEM registration.
tools.architecture: 2D U-Net trained for cross-modal image translation.
tools.training_data: Paired EM and FLM images of cell nuclei (HeLa, C. elegans, human skin) from the authors' lab.
tools.when_to_use: Automated 2D CLEM registration when chromatin stain is the fiducial; avoids manual fiducial picking.
tools.limitations: Trained mostly on nuclear/chromatin data; cross-domain generalization to other organelles or to cryo-CLEM unverified; 2D only.
tools.verification_notes: Seifert, Markert, Britz et al. F1000Research 9:1275 (2020), version 2 (2022).

tools.name: CLEM-Reg
tools.approach: napari-based automated registration for volume CLEM datasets. Builds two point clouds from organelle segmentations (e.g., mitochondria) in fluorescence and EM volumes, then uses probabilistic point-cloud registration (Coherent Point Drift / Bayesian CPD) to align them in 3D.
tools.architecture: ML-based segmentation backbones (Empanada / MitoNet for EM; spot/object detectors for FM) + probabilistic point-cloud registration.
tools.training_data: Crick benchmark vCLEM datasets; HeLa/SUM159 mitochondria.
tools.when_to_use: Volume CLEM where landmark beads are unavailable or sparse; especially useful when mitochondria, ER, or nuclei can be segmented in both modalities.
tools.limitations: Registration quality depends on segmentation quality of common structures; not designed for single-section CLEM; cryo-CLEM extension still in development.
tools.compute: Workstation with 1 GPU for segmentation; CPU sufficient for registration.
tools.verification_notes: Krentzel D, Elphick D, Domart MC, Larijani B, Heaysman C, Brito IL et al. Nat Methods (online 2025-09; PMID 40931193). Initial preprint bioRxiv 2023.05.11.540445 (Krentzel et al. 2023).

tools.name: BigWarp
tools.approach: BigDataViewer-based interactive landmark registration that builds a thin-plate-spline (TPS) warp from user-placed point correspondences between moving and target volumes; scales to terabyte-sized N5/Zarr datasets and integrates with Fiji and napari.
tools.architecture: Thin-plate-spline (Java)
tools.when_to_use: Manual or semi-automated CLEM/vEM registration at TB scale, especially for non-rigid alignment of FM to vEM volumes; common stepping stone before ML segmentation.
tools.limitations: Manual landmark placement is the rate-limiter; no automatic landmark detection built-in.
tools.compute: CPU + memory; very large datasets benefit from SSD.
tools.verification_notes: Bogovic JA, Hanslovsky P, Wong A, Saalfeld S. 'Robust registration of calcium images by learned contrast synthesis.' ISBI 2016; software canonical at saalfeldlab/bigwarp.

tools.name: ec-CLEM
tools.approach: Icy plugin for landmark- or automatic point-correspondence registration across CLEM modalities. Supports rigid, affine and non-rigid transformations across large scale and resolution gaps with statistical error estimation and deformation detection.
tools.architecture: Classical statistical landmark-based registration (no neural network)
tools.when_to_use: Default CLEM registration baseline (landmark-based) in Icy; appropriate for 2D and 3D, room-temperature and cryo-CLEM, where shared fiducials or recognisable features exist.
tools.limitations: Performance hinges on landmark quality/quantity; no ML-driven automatic detection of biological features; some deformations require manual correspondence.
tools.verification_notes: Paul-Gilloteaux P, Heiligenstein X, Belle M, Domart MC, Larijani B, Collinson L, Raposo G, Salamero J. Nat Methods 14(2):102-103 (2017). PMID 28139674.

tools.name: CryoVesNet
tools.approach: 3D U-Net (CARE-style blocks) trained on manually segmented neuronal cryo-tomograms followed by morphological post-processing (size/shape filtering, sphere-fitting) to give per-vesicle instance segmentations of round membrane-bound organelles. Designed for synaptic-vesicle pool quantification.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (CARE building blocks)
tools.training_data: Manually segmented rat synaptosome and primary neuronal-culture tomograms (Zuber lab).
tools.when_to_use: Quantitative analysis of synaptic vesicle pools, vesicle-membrane interactions; baseline for any round membrane-bound organelle in cryo-ET.
tools.limitations: Strongly tuned for spherical vesicles; non-vesicular round densities (e.g., dense-core LSDs) require retraining; sensitive to ice quality.
tools.verification_notes: Khosrozadeh A, Seeger R, Witz G, Radecke J, Sørensen JB, Zuber B. J Cell Biol 224(1):e202402169 (2025). PMID 39446113, DOI 10.1083/jcb.202402169.

tools.name: TARDIS-EM
tools.approach: Two-stage instance segmentation: a transformer-based deep-learning module produces semantic segmentation of filaments and membranes; a downstream geometric model resolves individual instances. Designed to operate dimensionlessly on both 2D micrographs and 3D tomograms.
tools.architecture: Transformer encoder + geometric instance-segmentation post-processing (point-cloud / graph-based); 'Dimensionless' refers to operating on 2D and 3D inputs through the same model class.
tools.training_data: Authors generated and released a large annotated dataset of microtubule and membrane segmentations across ~13,000 tomograms, now hosted on the CZII CryoET Data Portal. Ships with pretrained weights for microtubules and membranes; additional targets can be fine-tuned.
tools.when_to_use: Best when the chapter needs to discuss automated segmentation of filaments (microtubules in particular) and membranes in cellular cryo-ET tomograms or 2D micrographs, including via a napari plugin for interactive use.
tools.limitations: As of the 2024 preprint, primarily benchmarked on microtubule and membrane targets; generalisation to other filament classes (actin, intermediate filaments) and to densely packed mixed-target cryo-ET data still being characterised. Preprint at time of cataloging — confirm peer-reviewed publication before chapter submission.
tools.compute: GPU recommended; inference on a single workstation GPU is the documented use case (napari plugin runs locally).
tools.verification_notes: Citation verified against bioRxiv listing and PMC PMC11702698 (Dec 2024). Earlier conference companion: Kiewisz, Fabig, Müller-Reichert, Bepler (2023) 'Automated Segmentation of 3D Cytoskeletal Filaments from Electron Micrographs with TARDIS,' Microscopy and Microanalysis 29(Suppl_1):970. Refresh citation to peer-reviewed version when one appears.

tools.name: Ais
tools.approach: Unified GUI tool for cryo-ET segmentation: in-app annotation, CNN training, 3D visualisation, mesh/particle export.
tools.architecture: Various CNNs (U-Net, ResUNet) trained in-app
tools.training_data: User-supplied; ships pretrained models
tools.when_to_use: When you want an integrated GUI-driven cryo-ET segmentation workflow with model training built in (rather than scripting).
tools.limitations: GUI-first; less scriptable than membrain-seg/DeePiCt.
tools.verification_notes: eLife 2024; corrected author from query (Last, Abendstein, Voortman, Sharp; NOT van der Stam).

tools.name: MemBrain-seg
tools.approach: Generalist 3D U-Net membrane segmentation trained iteratively on diverse tomograms with a Surface-Dice loss that emphasises membrane connectivity; uses Fourier-based augmentations for adaptability.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (nnU-Net-style backbone)
tools.training_data: Iteratively expanded diverse tomogram set across yeast, mammalian, bacterial cells
tools.when_to_use: First-line membrane segmentation in cryo-ET, out-of-the-box on diverse data.
tools.limitations: Bright artefacts (gold) and thick ice can produce false membranes; refinement scripts recommended.
tools.compute: Single GPU (24 GB+ for full tomogram)
tools.verification_notes: Preprint only as of search date; peer-review status to be verified before chapter publication. | CORRECTION: Expert asked whether peer-reviewed version exists. Verification confirms it does not; only the bioRxiv preprint (v2) exists. Updated authorship and explicit confirmation in verification notes.

tools.name: TomoSegMemTV
tools.approach: Local Gaussian-like membrane model + tensor-voting that propagates anisotropic structural votes between voxels; bridges gaps and survives low SNR.
tools.architecture: Classical (no neural network)
tools.training_data: n/a
tools.when_to_use: When deterministic, parameter-tuned classical pipeline is preferred (no GPU, no training).
tools.limitations: Parameter tuning per dataset; slower than ML; less accurate on heterogeneous cellular context than MemBrain-seg.
tools.verification_notes: JSB 186:49-61 (2014); verified. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'processing'.

tools.name: Amira
tools.approach: Commercial GUI-driven platform for 3D/4D biological image analysis. Combines classical segmentation primitives (thresholding, watershed, region growing, manual painting), shallow ML (random forest / pixel classifier modules), and a deep-learning workroom for 2D/3D AI segmentation. Marketed for life sciences as Amira; the same code base ships as Avizo for materials science. Heavily used in volume EM (FIB-SEM, SBEM, ssTEM, array tomography) workflows that require interactive annotation plus quantitative analysis (volumetry, mesh extraction, connectivity, statistics).
tools.architecture: Platform — multiple algorithms; deep-learning modules wrap U-Net-style architectures, plus shallow ML (random-forest pixel classifiers à la ilastik/Weka style).
tools.training_paradigm: supervised (for the DL segmentation workroom); user provides annotations and trains in-product. Pretrained models for common targets are shipped/available depending on license tier.
tools.training_data: User-supplied annotations created within the Segmentation Workroom; no published canonical training set.
tools.when_to_use: Standard choice in many vEM and biomedical-imaging labs for interactive segmentation, quantitative 3D analysis, and publication-quality visualization. Best when manual oversight is needed, when a unified GUI across modalities is preferred over scripting, or when the workflow must combine vEM with adjacent modalities (LM, micro-CT). Less appropriate when the workflow needs full open-source reproducibility, headless batch processing on cluster GPUs, or cutting-edge ML methods that lag the commercial release.
tools.limitations: Closed-source and license-gated; pricing and feature gating restrict reproducibility in publications. ML modules trail open-source state of the art by a release cycle or more. No peer-reviewed methods paper — cite the vendor URL or pair with an open-source alternative when describing methodology. License terms can complicate sharing of trained models with collaborators.
tools.compute: Workstation-class CPU + mid-to-high-end GPU recommended for the DL workroom; routinely runs on a single workstation rather than a cluster.
tools.verification_notes: Vendor software with no canonical peer-reviewed methods paper. Cite via the Thermo Fisher product page (https://www.thermofisher.com/.../amira-software.html) and note in prose that it is commercial. Historical lineage: originally TGS / Visualization Sciences Group → FEI → acquired into Thermo Fisher Scientific.

tools.name: 3D U-Net
tools.approach: Volumetric segmentation U-Net learned from sparse annotations (annotate a few slices, network densely segments the volume); ancestor of nearly all 3D vEM networks.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (symmetric encoder-decoder with skip connections)
tools.training_data: Xenopus kidney confocal (original demonstration); used widely in EM by community since
tools.when_to_use: Reference 3D architecture; underlies almost every vEM and cryo-ET segmentation tool.
tools.limitations: Pure 3D U-Net is now superseded by nnU-Net's auto-config; cited for the architecture, not for direct use.
tools.verification_notes: MICCAI 2016; arXiv 1606.06650.

tools.name: Cellpose
tools.approach: Generalist cell segmentation predicting flow fields (gradient toward cell centre) plus a foreground mask; flows are integrated to recover cell instance boundaries. v2 adds human-in-the-loop fine-tuning; v3 adds one-click image restoration trained to optimise downstream segmentation.
tools.architecture: U-Net variant predicting horizontal/vertical flows + probability; v3 includes restoration head
tools.training_data: ~70,000 segmented cells across LM/EM modalities (v1); expanded in v2/v3
tools.when_to_use: First-line for cell-like segmentation across LM and many EM contexts; CLEM workflows for LM upstream.
tools.limitations: Designed primarily for cell-like blobs; struggles with non-cell EM features. v3 restoration may oversmooth.
tools.verification_notes: Cellpose 1: Stringer et al. 2021 Nat. Methods 18:100-106. Cellpose 2: Pachitariu & Stringer 2022 Nat. Methods 19:1634-1641 (DOI 10.1038/s41592-022-01663-4). Cellpose3: Stringer & Pachitariu 2025 Nat. Methods (DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02595-5).

tools.name: Cellpose-SAM
tools.approach: Cellpose framework with the SAM ViT backbone substituted as encoder; produces flow-field outputs while leveraging SAM's pretraining; designed for robustness to channel-shuffling, blur, noise, downsampling.
tools.architecture: SAM-derived ViT encoder + Cellpose flow-prediction decoder
tools.training_data: Cellpose corpus expanded with augmentations
tools.when_to_use: When you want a SAM-grade foundation backbone for cell segmentation with Cellpose's flow-based instance recovery.
tools.limitations: Preprint as of 2025-04; not yet peer-reviewed at search time. SAM-scale compute.
tools.verification_notes: Preprint only; verify peer-review status before chapter cite.

tools.name: DeepEMhancer
tools.approach: Deep-learning map post-processing: 3D CNN trained on pairs of experimental cryo-EM maps and atomic-model-derived sharpened maps; learns masking-like + sharpening-like operation in one step. Included here because the workflow is map-aware segmentation of map signal.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net
tools.training_data: Pairs (experimental EMDB map, atomic-model-derived sharpened map)
tools.when_to_use: Borderline placement: post-reconstruction map enhancement. Included here because it is a frequent companion to segmentation tasks (improves downstream map-to-model). Could equally appear under data_analysis.
tools.limitations: Over-sharpening risk; hallucination concern at low resolution.
tools.verification_notes: Comm. Biol. 4:874; included for completeness — primary placement may be data_analysis stage. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'data_analysis'.

tools.name: DINOv2
tools.approach: Self-supervised ViT pretrained by teacher-student distillation (iBOT + DINO + SwAV components) on 142M curated natural images; used as a frozen feature extractor.
tools.architecture: ViT-S/B/L/g (DINOv2-pretrained)
tools.training_data: LVD-142M (curated natural image dataset)
tools.when_to_use: As a frozen backbone for downstream EM tasks (linear probes, kNN). Increasingly used as feature extractor in cryo-EM pipelines (research-stage).
tools.limitations: Pretrained on natural images; EM transfer depends on task. Often outperformed on EM by domain-pretrained backbones (CEM500K-derived).

citation.venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR) / arXiv 2304.07193

tools.name: Ilastik
tools.approach: Interactive random-forest classifier on pre-computed multi-scale image features; user paints labels and the model trains on-the-fly. Workflows for pixel/object classification, counting, tracking.
tools.architecture: Random forest on hand-crafted image features (later optional deep-learning workflow)
tools.training_data: User-supplied scribble labels
tools.when_to_use: First-line for small-data interactive segmentation; common in vEM pre-deep-learning era; still useful as fast prototype tool.
tools.limitations: Random-forest features limit accuracy on complex structures; deep-learning workflow exists but less integrated.
tools.verification_notes: Nat. Methods 16:1226-1232; verified.

tools.name: MicroSAM
tools.approach: SAM fine-tuned on light and electron microscopy data; provides interactive (click/box prompt) and automatic segmentation, plus 3D and tracking via napari plugin.
tools.architecture: SAM (ViT-B/L/H) fine-tuned on microscopy
tools.training_data: Curated LM and EM dataset (mixture of public; details in paper)
tools.when_to_use: Interactive annotation acceleration on novel data with little/no training; volumetric segmentation via SAM 2 backbone.
tools.limitations: Prompt-dependent quality; zero-shot on high-resolution SPA-class features can over-segment.
tools.verification_notes: PMC11903314; verified.

tools.name: nnU-Net
tools.approach: Self-configuring U-Net pipeline: automatically adapts preprocessing, network depth/topology, training schedule, and post-processing to a given dataset using fingerprinting.
tools.architecture: 2D / 3D U-Net (Cicek-style) with auto-configured depth & feature counts
tools.training_data: Per-task (user supplies labels); benchmarked across 23 public datasets
tools.when_to_use: Strong baseline whenever you have labelled vEM data; the canonical 'just use nnU-Net' choice.
tools.limitations: Auto-config is opinionated; harder to deviate from defaults. Doesn't innovate architecturally beyond U-Net family.
tools.verification_notes: Nat. Methods 18:203-211; verified.

tools.name: SAM 2
tools.approach: Successor to SAM with streaming memory enabling video / volumetric segmentation; 6x faster, 3x fewer interactions for video.
tools.architecture: ViT image encoder + memory bank + mask decoder; streaming transformer architecture
tools.training_data: SA-V: ~50.9k videos, ~643k masklets (natural video)
tools.when_to_use: Volumetric EM segmentation by treating z-slices as video frames; integrated by MicroSAM 3D mode.
tools.limitations: Volume propagation can drift across slices with large appearance changes; finetuning on EM strongly improves quality.
tools.verification_notes: arXiv 2408.00714; ICLR 2025 proceedings.

tools.name: Segment Anything Model (SAM)
tools.approach: Promptable segmentation: ViT image encoder + prompt encoder (clicks/boxes/masks) + mask decoder; trained on 1B masks across 11M natural images.
tools.architecture: ViT-B/L/H image encoder + transformer-based mask decoder
tools.training_data: SA-1B: 1.1B masks on 11M images (natural, not microscopy)
tools.when_to_use: Zero/few-shot interactive segmentation backbone for many EM tools (MicroSAM, Cellpose-SAM, CryoSegNet).
tools.limitations: Out-of-the-box on EM data over-segments / merges adjacent structures; usually wants fine-tuning.
tools.verification_notes: ICCV 2023; arXiv 2304.02643; verified.

tools.name: Stardist
tools.approach: Per-pixel object probability + radial distances to a star-convex polygon (2D) / polyhedron (3D); NMS-style selection yields instances.
tools.architecture: U-Net predicting (object probability, radial-distance vector)
tools.training_data: Histopathology, fluorescence nuclei datasets; 3D extension on confocal/EM
tools.when_to_use: Convex/quasi-convex nuclei or cells; widely used in LM and applicable to LM side of CLEM.
tools.limitations: Star-convex assumption breaks for highly concave structures.
tools.verification_notes: MICCAI 2018; 3D extension Weigert 2020 WACV.

tools.name: CryoSAM
tools.approach: Training-free framework that adapts the 2D SAM foundation model to cryo-ET tomograms via cross-plane self-prompting (propagating prompts through orthogonal slices to do 3D instance segmentation recursively) and hierarchical feature matching for one-prompt full-tomogram semantic segmentation.
tools.architecture: SAM (ViT-H) + cross-plane prompt-propagation module + hierarchical feature matcher.
tools.training_data: n/a (no per-task training); evaluated on EMPIAR cryo-ET datasets.
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-ET segmentation tasks with very few labels; rapid exploratory annotation in napari/ChimeraX.
tools.limitations: Reuses SAM's natural-image priors; performance degrades on small/round particles with low contrast; hyperparameters per feature class.
tools.compute: GPU with >=24 GB VRAM (SAM ViT-H inference is heavy).
tools.verification_notes: Zhao Y, Bian H, Mu M et al. 'CryoSAM: Training-Free CryoET Tomogram Segmentation with Foundation Models.' MICCAI 2024. CMU / UAB authorship.

tools.name: DeepETPicker
tools.approach: 3D ResUNet segmentation network trained with weakly-supervised simplified labels; outputs voxel probability maps that are post-processed to particle coordinates.
tools.architecture: 3D ResUNet
tools.training_data: Sparsely labelled tomograms with simple sphere labels
tools.when_to_use: Faster alternative to DeepFinder with reduced labelling burden; reported best overall accuracy on simulated and real test sets.
tools.limitations: Weak supervision still requires some labelled particles per class.
tools.verification_notes: PMC11258139; Nat. Commun. 15:2090; verified.

tools.name: DeepFinder
tools.approach: 3D CNN that simultaneously localises and classifies multiple macromolecule classes in cellular tomograms; outputs a per-voxel class probability map.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (multi-class segmentation), with mean-shift clustering of class probability volumes to extract centres
tools.training_data: Cellular tomograms with expert annotations for ribosomes, RuBisCO, PSII etc.; SHREC simulated data for benchmarks
tools.when_to_use: Multi-class macromolecule localisation in cellular cryo-ET when retraining on labelled tomograms is feasible.
tools.limitations: Needs per-class labelled training tomograms; performance sinks on small particles (<~200 kDa); class imbalance issues.
tools.compute: Single GPU (24 GB recommended for full tomograms)
tools.verification_notes: Verified: SHREC top performer; Nature Methods 18:1386-1394 (2021).

tools.name: DeePiCt
tools.approach: Two-stage 2D + 3D CNN combination for joint organelle segmentation and particle picking; 2D net segments cellular context (membranes, organelles), 3D net picks particles.
tools.architecture: 2D U-Net (context) + 3D U-Net (particle)
tools.training_data: 20 expert-annotated S. pombe tomograms (ribosomes, FAS, membranes, NPCs, organelles)
tools.when_to_use: When you need both organelle context (membranes, nuclei, mitochondria) and particle picks in one pipeline.
tools.limitations: S. pombe-trained models; degrades on non-yeast cellular context. Annotation requirements high.
tools.compute: Single GPU; 24-48 GB VRAM for full-volume
tools.verification_notes: PMC PubMed 36690741; verified.

tools.name: Dynamo template matching
tools.approach: Classical 3D cross-correlation template matching; geometry-aware (uses surface, membrane, helical priors) plus GPU acceleration.
tools.architecture: Classical FFT correlation; recent geometry-aware variants
tools.training_data: n/a
tools.when_to_use: Within Dynamo workflows for subtomogram averaging; especially with strong geometric priors (vesicle, filament).
tools.limitations: Matlab dependency; template bias; tuning required.
tools.verification_notes: Castano-Diez 2012 JSB 178:139-151; recent update Lopez-Soto 2025 Structure (DOI 10.1016/j.str.2025.x).

tools.name: EMAN2 tomogram CNN segmentation
tools.approach: Small CNN trained on ~10 manually-annotated 64x64 tiles from a single tomogram to segment cellular features (membranes, microtubules, ribosomes); used both for segmentation and as a precursor to particle picking.
tools.architecture: Small 2D CNN run on tomogram slices
tools.training_data: User-supplied (a few annotated tiles)
tools.when_to_use: Quick interactive segmentation of features in EMAN2; baseline for in-tomogram ML.
tools.limitations: Per-tomogram retraining; modest accuracy compared to 3D U-Net pipelines.

tools.name: emClarity template matching
tools.approach: GPU-accelerated 3D template matching as the picking step of the emClarity STA pipeline; includes 3D-sampling-function-compensated classification.
tools.architecture: Classical GPU TM
tools.training_data: n/a
tools.when_to_use: When in the emClarity STA workflow; particularly strong on high-resolution targets like ribosomes.
tools.limitations: Matlab dependency; learning curve.
tools.verification_notes: Nat. Methods 15:955-961; verified.

tools.name: MemBrain-pick
tools.approach: Picks membrane-bound particles by extracting and orienting subvolumes along a segmented membrane; trains a regression network to predict particle-to-nearest-particle distance (rather than binary class).
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net / regression CNN over membrane-aligned subvolumes
tools.training_data: 28 in-house annotated membrane tomograms (Plitzko / Mahamid lab)
tools.when_to_use: Specifically for membrane-embedded proteins where orientation along the membrane is needed.
tools.limitations: Requires a good membrane segmentation upstream (use MemBrain-seg).

citation.venue: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine

tools.verification_notes: Lamm 2022 CMPB; MemBrain v2 preprint bioRxiv 2024.01.05.574336 (Lamm et al.) covers updates.

tools.name: PickYOLO
tools.approach: YOLO-style fast 3D-aware particle detector for cryo-ET tomograms; trained on few hundred annotated particle centres.
tools.architecture: YOLO-style CNN detector adapted for tomogram slices/sub-volumes
tools.training_data: Few hundred labelled particles from a single tomogram
tools.when_to_use: When throughput matters; reported 0.24-3.75 s/tomogram inference.
tools.limitations: Class-aware: needs retraining per particle class. Less robust than TomoTwin to unseen classes.
tools.verification_notes: JSB 215(3):107990 verified; authors Genthe, Miletic, Tekkali, Hennell James, Marlovits, Heuser.

tools.name: PySeg
tools.approach: Graph- and discrete-Morse-theory based pipeline for tracing densities protruding from segmented membranes in cryo-tomograms, followed by rotational-average-based 2D classification and de novo subtomogram averaging. Pipeline-agnostic with respect to upstream membrane segmentation.
tools.architecture: Classical morphological + graph algorithms (Disperse / discrete Morse complex)
tools.when_to_use: Workhorse for template-free picking of membrane-embedded/anchored complexes (ribosomes-on-ER, viral spikes, synaptic clefts) in cellular cryo-ET.
tools.limitations: Sensitive to membrane-segmentation quality; many heuristic parameters; classification step requires manual curation.
tools.compute: CPU-bound; large memory for whole-tomogram graphs.
tools.verification_notes: Martinez-Sanchez A, Kochovski Z, Laugks U et al. Nat Methods 17:209-216 (2020). PMID 31907446, DOI 10.1038/s41592-019-0675-5. Currently only listed as an integration target in the catalog; promote to a top-level entry.

tools.name: PyTOM-Match-Pick
tools.approach: GPU-accelerated 3D template matching with extensive angular sampling; recent version adds top-hat-transform constraint to reduce false positives in classification.
tools.architecture: Classical GPU FFT-based 3D cross-correlation
tools.training_data: n/a
tools.when_to_use: When a high-quality template is available (e.g., ribosome) and classical TM with explicit angular sampling is preferred.
tools.limitations: Template bias; sensitive to angular sampling; slower than ML.
tools.verification_notes: Two papers: Chaillet 2023 IJMS, Chaillet 2025 JSB:X (DOI 10.1016/j.yjsbx.2025.100125). The Förster group at Utrecht.

tools.name: TomoTwin
tools.approach: Deep metric-learning (triplet/contrastive) that maps tomogram sub-volumes to a 32-D embedding space where macromolecules cluster by 3D structure; picks class-agnostically via reference embeddings.
tools.architecture: 3D CNN encoder trained with metric-learning (triplet) loss; ~120 simulated proteins as anchors
tools.training_data: Simulated tomograms of 120 different proteins (synthetic from PDB)
tools.when_to_use: When you want class-agnostic picking without retraining per particle, or to discover unknown macromolecules in cellular tomograms.
tools.limitations: Trained on simulated tomograms; performance varies on real cellular tomograms; small/asymmetric particles harder.
tools.verification_notes: Nat. Methods 20:871-880; verified.

tools.name: APPLE-picker
tools.approach: Template-free, training-free picker based on a query-image vs reference-region distance metric; uses simple statistical descriptors.
tools.architecture: Statistical / classical (no neural network)
tools.training_data: n/a (no training)
tools.when_to_use: When you want a no-training picker with predictable behavior; baseline for SPA picking comparison.
tools.limitations: Less accurate than ML pickers on noisy/heterogeneous data.

tools.name: CASSPER
tools.approach: Semantic-segmentation network (pixel-level classification) that distinguishes protein, ice, carbon, and contamination using CLAHE-preprocessed micrographs; particles extracted from protein masks.
tools.architecture: Encoder-decoder semantic segmentation CNN (DenseNet-style backbone)
tools.training_data: Visually-prepared mask labels on small in-house and EMPIAR set
tools.when_to_use: When ice/contamination masking is itself useful (downstream quality filtering).
tools.limitations: Semantic segmentation slower than YOLO; manual mask annotation more onerous than box labels.
tools.verification_notes: PMC7884729; verified.

tools.name: Cryo-EMMAE
tools.approach: Self-supervised masked-autoencoder pretraining on cryo-EM micrographs; particles identified by clustering the learned latent representations (no manual labels).
tools.architecture: Masked autoencoder (MAE) with ViT backbone + clustering head
tools.training_data: Diverse EMPIAR micrographs (unlabelled)
tools.when_to_use: When you have novel specimens with no labels; reported to converge with as few as 5 micrographs.
tools.limitations: Recent; limited independent validation. First-author and venue verified, but adoption metrics not yet established.
tools.verification_notes: PMC12296464; PubMed 40628274. First-author name verified to be Cuevas-Saavedra et al. (the actual byline should be confirmed against the published paper before citation in the chapter).

tools.name: crYOLO
tools.approach: YOLO-based deep object detector trained on micrograph patches; outputs bounding boxes for particles. Ships a general model pretrained on >60 datasets that often works zero-shot.
tools.architecture: YOLOv2/v3-style single-shot CNN detector (Darknet-19 / -53 backbone, ~30 conv layers)
tools.training_data: Initial paper: ~5 training datasets, 200-2500 particles each; general model trained on >60 datasets spanning soluble, membrane, filamentous proteins. Most datasets are EMPIAR entries plus in-house Raunser-lab data.
tools.when_to_use: First-line SPA picker on commodity GPU; general model means no training in many cases. Filament picking supported via dedicated mode.
tools.limitations: Bounding-box detection assumes globular shape; struggles with very small (<70 kDa) particles in thin ice. Pretrained model degrades on highly novel shapes (small ssRNA, very thin filaments).
tools.compute: Single GPU (8-24 GB VRAM); training fast (minutes on modern GPU); inference ~5 micrographs/s
tools.verification_notes: Wagner 2020 follow-up (Commun. Biol., DOI 10.1038/s42003-020-0790-y) extends to filaments and general model. Both papers verified on Nature site.

tools.name: CryoSegNet
tools.approach: Two-stage pipeline: attention-gated U-Net trained on cryo-EM to generate intermediate input for SAM, which then performs final particle segmentation.
tools.architecture: Attention-gated U-Net + SAM (ViT-H backbone)
tools.training_data: CryoPPP
tools.when_to_use: When seeking SAM-augmented picking; reported 7% / 14% resolution improvement over Topaz / crYOLO on Cheng-lab tests.
tools.limitations: Pipeline complexity; SAM inference cost; ground-truth comparison only on CryoPPP-like data.
tools.verification_notes: PMC11165428; verified.

tools.name: CryoTransformer
tools.approach: Transformer-based object detector built on top of a ResNet feature extractor; trained on the CryoPPP large labelled dataset.
tools.architecture: DETR-style transformer detector with ResNet backbone
tools.training_data: CryoPPP (Dhakal et al. 2023): 34 protein datasets, ~9,893 micrographs
tools.when_to_use: When a transformer-class model with large pretraining (CryoPPP) is desired; reported FSC improvements over crYOLO/Topaz on Cheng-lab benchmark.
tools.limitations: Transformer detectors slower than YOLO at inference; generalization beyond CryoPPP distribution not extensively reported.
tools.verification_notes: PMC10937899; verified.

tools.name: DeepCryoPicker
tools.approach: Unsupervised candidate-generation pipeline (clustering) + supervised CNN classifier on candidates.
tools.architecture: Custom CNN classifier on candidate patches
tools.training_data: EMPIAR sets (auto-labelled then verified)
tools.when_to_use: Historical entry; minimally maintained.
tools.limitations: Reliant on quality of unsupervised candidate generation.
tools.verification_notes: BMC Bioinformatics 21(1):509 verified.

tools.name: DeepPicker
tools.approach: Sliding-window CNN classifier; introduced cross-molecule training to learn shared particle features across datasets.
tools.architecture: 8-layer CNN (early VGG-style) classifier on cropped patches
tools.training_data: Three EMPIAR complexes, sliding-window labels
tools.when_to_use: Historical baseline; rarely first choice today.
tools.limitations: Sliding-window approach is slow; produces many false positives; largely superseded by crYOLO/Topaz.

tools.name: DRPnet
tools.approach: Two-stage: fully-convolutional regression network (FCRN) regresses a particle-center distance map; second CNN classifies refined candidates.
tools.architecture: FCRN (U-Net-like) + classification CNN
tools.training_data: Hand-labelled EMPIAR datasets
tools.when_to_use: Heatmap-based picking when regression-style outputs are preferred.
tools.limitations: Less widely adopted than crYOLO/Topaz.
tools.verification_notes: BMC Bioinformatics 22:55; verified.

tools.name: EMAN2 NN-picker
tools.approach: Stack of small CNNs trained on user-provided positive/negative micrograph patches; designed for interactive use within EMAN2.
tools.architecture: Small stacked CNN (custom, not deep)
tools.training_data: User-supplied; few hundred patches per session
tools.when_to_use: If already in EMAN2 workflow and want interactive training.
tools.limitations: No pretrained general model; per-dataset training. Quality lower than crYOLO/Topaz on standard SPA.
tools.verification_notes: Part of Bell et al. 2018 'New software tools in EMAN2 inspired by EMDatabank map challenge'.

tools.name: EPicker
tools.approach: Exemplar-based continual-learning picker; accumulates knowledge from many small datasets without catastrophic forgetting. Supports particles, vesicles, fibers.
tools.architecture: CNN detector with continual-learning replay buffer
tools.training_data: Multiple cryo-EM datasets accumulated over time
tools.when_to_use: When picking diverse object types (particles, vesicles, fibers) with a single accumulating model.
tools.limitations: Continual-learning quality depends on replay strategy; less widely adopted than crYOLO/Topaz.
tools.verification_notes: PMC9072698; verified.

tools.name: Gautomatch
tools.approach: GPU-accelerated template- or template-free cross-correlation picker.
tools.architecture: Classical cross-correlation on GPU
tools.training_data: n/a
tools.when_to_use: When templates available and GPU CC desired; long the default first-pass picker before crYOLO/Topaz era.
tools.limitations: No peer-reviewed paper; closed-source binary distribution. Maintenance unclear.
tools.verification_notes: No canonical paper found; widely cited via Zhang K. (unpublished). This must be flagged in chapter — UNVERIFIED publication.

tools.name: PIXER
tools.approach: Semantic-segmentation network outputs a probability density map of pixel-wise particle membership; local maxima -> particle centers.
tools.architecture: Encoder-decoder segmentation CNN
tools.training_data: Auto-generated segmentation training set from labelled coords
tools.when_to_use: Historical baseline showing semantic-segmentation framing predates CASSPER.
tools.limitations: Limited maintenance.
tools.verification_notes: PMC6339297; verified.

tools.name: REPIC
tools.approach: Consensus / ensemble methodology that combines outputs from multiple pickers (crYOLO, Topaz, Warp etc.) via integer-linear-programming graph matching. Not a picker itself but a meta-picker.
tools.architecture: Classical ILP optimization on bipartite particle-match graph
tools.training_data: n/a (uses already-trained pickers)
tools.when_to_use: When you have run multiple pickers and want a principled consensus rather than majority vote.
tools.limitations: ILP cost scales with particle count; adds complexity to workflow.
tools.verification_notes: PMC11528043; verified.

tools.name: Template matching (RELION / cryoSPARC)
tools.approach: 2D cross-correlation against a (low-pass-filtered) 2D template; picks local maxima above threshold.
tools.architecture: Classical FFT-based correlation
tools.training_data: n/a
tools.when_to_use: Required when a high-quality 2D average is available; still the default for some workflows in RELION/cryoSPARC.
tools.limitations: Template bias (Einstein-from-noise risk if threshold too low); poor performance on small/low-contrast particles.
tools.verification_notes: RELION reference (Scheres 2015); cryoSPARC reference Punjani et al. 2017 Nat. Methods (separate entry).

tools.name: Topaz
tools.approach: Convolutional neural network trained with positive-unlabeled (PU) learning; small set of labelled particles plus unlabelled micrograph regions. Includes 2D/3D denoising sub-modules.
tools.architecture: ResNet-style CNN classifier on sliding windows; loss is PU-learning approximation of risk on unlabelled data
tools.training_data: Several EMPIAR sets (T20S proteasome EMPIAR-10025, others) plus in-house; documented use with as few as a few hundred particles
tools.when_to_use: When you have sparse labels and want a picker that explicitly handles partial annotation noise; small/non-globular particles where bounding boxes fail.
tools.limitations: PU-learning requires honest prior on positive class fraction; mis-set prior leads to over/under-picking. Newer versions sometimes lag in maintenance.
tools.compute: Single GPU (8-16 GB); CPU inference possible but slow
tools.verification_notes: Verified PubMed PMC6858545; arXiv preprint 1803.08207.

tools.name: UPicker
tools.approach: Semi-supervised transformer-based detector that exploits unlabelled micrographs alongside small labelled set.
tools.architecture: DETR-style detection transformer with semi-supervised pseudo-labelling
tools.training_data: Mix of labelled and unlabelled cryo-EM micrographs (CryoPPP / EMPIAR)
tools.when_to_use: When labelled data is scarce and large pools of unlabelled micrographs exist.
tools.limitations: Semi-supervised quality sensitive to pseudo-label noise; recent so adoption nascent.
tools.verification_notes: PMC11631311; verified.

tools.name: Warp / BoxNet
tools.approach: BoxNet is a 72-layer fully convolutional ResNet that performs semantic segmentation of micrographs into three pixel classes (background, particle, artifact); particle positions extracted as connected-component centers.
tools.architecture: ResNet-style 72-layer FCN (TensorFlow implementation)
tools.training_data: EMPIAR public data plus PDB-derived synthetic micrographs simulated across MW 0.064-18 MDa
tools.when_to_use: Real-time on-the-fly picking integrated with motion correction and CTF; in the cryo-ET version, BoxNet variants apply to 2D projections.
tools.limitations: BoxNet pretrained model can pick artifacts as particles on unusual grids; retraining ~10 min on representative set typically required.
tools.compute: Single GPU (12-24 GB VRAM) for inference; retraining on commodity GPU
tools.repo: http://www.warpem.com (Tegunov; standalone Windows app); Warp 2 (Linux/CUDA) rewritten 2023-2024
tools.verification_notes: PMC6858868; BoxNet is one module of the Warp suite.

tools.name: cryo-CARE
tools.approach: Noise2Noise-style content-aware denoising: trains a U-Net to map one noisy realization (even-frame sum or even-frame tomogram) to a paired independent noisy realization (odd-frame sum/tomogram), exploiting independence of shot noise between halves.
tools.architecture: 2D and 3D U-Net (encoder-decoder CNN with skip connections; CARE/CSBDeep lineage).
tools.training_data: Even/odd movie-frame splits of the user's own dataset; no external labels.
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-ET tomogram visualization and downstream segmentation; SPA micrograph denoising for visualization (not for downstream refinement, which would risk FSC inflation).
tools.limitations: Requires paired even/odd realizations; risks artificially correlating half-maps if used inside the SPA refinement loop; visual improvement does not guarantee resolution gain.
tools.compute: Single GPU; 8-24 GB VRAM depending on patch size.
tools.verification_notes: Buchholz T-O, Jordan M, Pigino G, Jug F. Proc. IEEE ISBI 2019:502-506 verified DOI 10.1109/ISBI.2019.8759519; arXiv 1810.05420.

tools.name: DenoisET
tools.approach: Noise2Noise implementation tailored to cryo-ET tomograms; designed for live-acquisition integration with AreTomo3/AreTomoLive: it auto-selects training tomograms and transitions from training to inference during streaming acquisition.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (Noise2Noise objective).
tools.training_data: Even/odd tomogram reconstructions emitted by AreTomo3 during acquisition.
tools.when_to_use: Live cryo-ET acquisition at facilities running AreTomoLive; alternative to cryoCARE-tomo with simpler integration.
tools.limitations: Preprint-stage at time of writing; tied to AreTomo3 outputs; no large-scale validation outside the AreTomoLive paper.
tools.verification_notes: DenoisET appears to lack a dedicated standalone paper; described in the AreTomoLive preprint (Peck A et al., 2025). Verify the AreTomoLive citation before chapter inclusion.

tools.name: JANNI
tools.approach: Noise2Noise CNN denoiser trained at MPI Dortmund on a pool of public cryo-EM movie pairs; ships a general pretrained model and is used as a visualization aid inside crYOLO and SPHIRE.
tools.architecture: U-Net (Keras/TensorFlow).
tools.training_data: Curated MPI-Dortmund/SPHIRE corpus of cryo-EM movie even/odd pairs across multiple EMPIAR samples.
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-EM micrograph denoising for visualization and as input to crYOLO when raw SNR is low.
tools.limitations: JANNI itself does not have a dedicated peer-reviewed paper; described in the SPHIRE-crYOLO Communications Biology paper. Pretrained model biased toward holey carbon SPA grids.
tools.verification_notes: Wagner T et al. (2020) Commun Biol 3:61 verified PMID 32047220 / DOI 10.1038/s42003-020-0790-y. JANNI is a companion tool released alongside SPHIRE-crYOLO 1.5; no JANNI-only paper exists.

tools.name: Noise2Noise
tools.approach: Foundational training paradigm: learn to denoise by mapping one noisy realization of a signal to another noisy realization; with zero-mean independent noise the L2-trained network converges toward the clean signal in expectation. Underlies cryo-CARE and Topaz-Denoise.
tools.architecture: Generic CNN/U-Net (architecture-agnostic; the contribution is the loss/training scheme).
tools.training_data: Paired noisy realizations of the same image; in cryo-EM these are even/odd movie-frame sums or even/odd tomograms.
tools.when_to_use: Reference for the training paradigm; not used directly in cryo-EM but cited as the methodological foundation of cryoCARE, Topaz-Denoise, JANNI, and DenoisET.
tools.limitations: Requires that the noise across realizations is independent and zero-mean; violated when even/odd halves are correlated through shared imaging artifacts.
tools.compute: Single GPU; reference implementation in TensorFlow.
tools.verification_notes: Lehtinen J et al. ICML 2018 (PMLR 80) verified arXiv 1803.04189; the proceedings entry is the canonical citation.

tools.name: Noise2Self
tools.approach: Self-supervised denoising via 'J-invariance': partitions pixels into groups and trains the network to predict each group from the others, so the predicted output is independent of the held-out group. Generalizes N2V and applies to any denoising function (not just CNNs).
tools.architecture: Architecture-agnostic (CNN, ViT, median filter all permitted); reference uses U-Net.
tools.training_data: The user's own noisy stack.
tools.when_to_use: Methodological reference; occasionally used in vEM denoising pipelines and single-cell imaging.
tools.limitations: Requires correct partition into J-invariant groups; assumes noise independence across groups.
tools.verification_notes: Batson J & Royer L. ICML 2019 (PMLR 97) verified arXiv 1901.11365.

tools.name: Noise2Void
tools.approach: Blind-spot self-supervised denoising: at each training step a random pixel is masked and the network is trained to predict it from its neighborhood. Eliminates the need for paired data; assumes pixel-independent noise.
tools.architecture: Generic 2D/3D U-Net (CSBDeep/JUG-lab implementation).
tools.training_data: The user's own noisy stack; no labels and no pairs.
tools.when_to_use: When paired noisy realizations are unavailable, e.g. legacy datasets without even/odd splits or single-tilt vEM stacks.
tools.limitations: Assumes spatially uncorrelated noise (often violated in EM after motion correction or detector binning); typically weaker than Noise2Noise when pairs are available.
tools.verification_notes: Krull A, Buchholz T-O, Jug F. CVPR 2019:2129-2137 verified.

tools.name: REST
tools.approach: Supervised translation from low-quality to high-quality density: a 3D CNN learns a mapping where the high-quality target is a sub-tomogram-averaged class average and the low-quality input is the raw extracted sub-tomogram; transfer to the whole tomogram for denoising and missing-wedge compensation.
tools.architecture: Custom 3D encoder-decoder with residual blocks.
tools.training_data: Sub-tomogram pairs of (raw, averaged class) for one or several target macromolecules; e.g. nucleosomes in cryo-FIB nuclei sections.
tools.when_to_use: When the user has a well-averaged structure for the target macromolecule and wants to inspect per-particle states without explicit STA.
tools.limitations: Requires a target structure to define 'clean'; risk of biasing tomograms toward the training class.
tools.verification_notes: Zhang H, Li Y, Liu Y et al. Nat Commun 14:2937 (2023) verified PMID 37217501.

tools.name: Topaz-Denoise
tools.approach: General-purpose deep denoiser for cryo-EM micrographs (2D) and cryo-ET tomograms (3D); supervised on real even/odd splits and synthetic noise pairs across many EMPIAR datasets; ships pretrained 2D and 3D models that can be applied zero-shot.
tools.architecture: 2D U-Net (Affine-NN encoder) and 3D U-Net variants.
tools.training_data: Thousands of micrographs across EMPIAR plus in-house data; for 3D, paired even/odd reconstructions from a curated set of tomograms.
tools.when_to_use: Drop-in pretrained denoising for visualization, particle picking aids, and downstream segmentation; particularly useful when paired even/odd realizations are not available.
tools.limitations: Models can over-smooth high-frequency biological signal; not validated by downstream FSC for SPA refinement; pretrained corpus may underrepresent membrane proteins or unusual grid types.
tools.compute: Single GPU; <=8 GB VRAM for 2D, 16+ GB for 3D.
tools.verification_notes: Bepler T, Kelley K, Noble AJ, Berger B. Nat Commun 11:5208 (2020) verified PMID 33060581 / DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-18952-1. | CORRECTION: Expert flagged the 3D Topaz-Denoise variant as missing. Verification: the 3D mode is in the same Bepler et al. 2020 Nat Commun paper as the 2D mode, not a separate publication. Update existing entry instead of creating a new one.

tools.name: DeepDeWedge
tools.approach: Self-supervised joint denoising and missing-wedge filling. A randomly-initialized 3D U-Net is fit per tomogram with a self-supervised loss that uses both even/odd subsets of tilts and synthetic wedge masking; combines Noise2Noise and missing-wedge-masking objectives.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net.
tools.training_data: Two reconstructions from disjoint tilt subsets of the same tomogram (no external labels).
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-ET tomograms with extreme missing-wedge artifacts where IsoNet under-performs; particularly for thick in-situ samples.
tools.limitations: Per-tomogram fit (no pretrained weights); hallucination warning identical to IsoNet; runtime can be hours.
tools.compute: GPU with 24+ GB VRAM for typical tomograms.
tools.verification_notes: Wiedemann S & Heckel R. Nat Commun 15:8255 (2024) verified DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-51438-y; arXiv 2311.05539. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'data_analysis'.

tools.name: IsoNet
tools.approach: Iterative deep learning for joint missing-wedge restoration and denoising of single cryo-ET tomograms. Trains a 3D U-Net to predict full-tomogram structure from versions in which a synthetic wedge has been masked; the network learns to fill in missing Fourier directions from features observed elsewhere in the same tomogram.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (Cicek-style) with custom missing-wedge masking loss.
tools.training_data: The user's own tomograms with synthetic wedge masking (no external labels). Authors validate on HIV, paraflagellar rod, neuronal-synapse tomograms.
tools.when_to_use: Cryo-ET visualization and segmentation when missing-wedge artifacts dominate; particularly useful before MemBrain-seg or DeePiCt.
tools.limitations: Iterative training is slow; hallucination risk (features may be reinforced); not used for sub-tomogram averaging (the wedge cannot be 'restored' for STA in a statistically meaningful way).
tools.compute: GPU with 16-24 GB VRAM; iterative training can take hours per tomogram.
tools.verification_notes: Liu Y-T, Zhang H, Wang H, Tao C-L, Bi G-Q, Zhou ZH. Nat Commun 13:6482 (2022) verified DOI 10.1038/s41467-022-33957-8. | DUP: canonical entry in stage 'data_analysis'.

tools.name: MWR (Missing Wedge Restoration)
tools.approach: Deep-learning missing-wedge fill predecessor to IsoNet, using a 3D U-Net trained on a small set of simulated tomograms to predict isotropic volumes from anisotropic input.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net trained with synthetic ground-truth pairs.
tools.training_data: Simulated cryo-ET volumes from atomic models; small dataset.
tools.when_to_use: Cited as an early baseline; largely superseded by IsoNet and DeepDeWedge for practical use.
tools.limitations: Trained on simulated data only; limited generalization; modest community uptake.
tools.verification_notes: Ding G, Liu Y, Zhang R, Xin HL. Commun Biol 2:483 (2019). PMID 31840079, DOI 10.1038/s42003-019-0660-7 verified (different MWR-style approach from later DeepDeWedge).

tools.name: BioImage Model Zoo
tools.approach: Community resource that distributes standardized, versioned deep-learning models for bioimage analysis under a common spec (RDF YAML) so that the same weights run in ilastik, deepImageJ, ZeroCostDL4Mic, ImJoy, QuPath, napari, StarDist, CSBDeep, etc.
tools.architecture: n/a (model registry + spec)
tools.training_data: n/a
tools.when_to_use: Anywhere a pretrained vEM / cryo-EM segmentation or denoising model needs to be shared or consumed across heterogeneous user-facing tools; reproducibility infrastructure for the chapter.
tools.limitations: Coverage of cryo-ET / cryo-EM models is still uneven; spec evolves rapidly.
tools.compute: Inference cost dictated by the model, not the registry.
tools.verification_notes: Ouyang W et al. bioRxiv 2022.06.07.495102 (2022). Still preprint as of 2026-05; consortium paper update expected.

tools.name: CEM500K
tools.approach: 500K-image cellular-EM dataset for self-supervised pretraining (curated from ~600 3D + ~10000 2D EM volumes). Released pretrained MoCoV2-style backbones for transfer to downstream segmentation.
tools.architecture: ResNet-50 backbone pretrained via MoCoV2 contrastive learning
tools.training_data: CEM500K: 0.5M unique 2D EM patches from heterogeneous cellular EM imaging projects
tools.when_to_use: When fine-tuning a vEM segmentation network with limited domain labels; canonical EM-domain pretraining.
tools.limitations: Largely mammalian cellular EM (HeLa, neurons); transfer to bacterial/plant/cryo-ET varies. Pre-SAM era backbone.

tools.name: CryoET Data Portal
tools.approach: Open repository of standardized cryo-ET tomograms and annotations, exposed via GraphQL API and Python client; serves both as a community benchmark (CZII Object Identification Kaggle challenge 2024-2025) and as the substrate for foundation-model training pipelines.
tools.architecture: n/a (data infrastructure); hosts model outputs and competition baselines
tools.when_to_use: Any 2024-2026 cryo-ET ML project that needs training data, benchmark splits, or community baselines; reference resource for chapter discussion of data infrastructure.
tools.limitations: Annotation density varies across datasets; not all entries are equally curated; user contributions are reviewed.
tools.compute: n/a (web service); local compute for downstream training.
tools.verification_notes: Ermel U, Peck A, Yu Y, et al. 'Annotating CryoET Volumes: A Machine Learning Challenge.' bioRxiv 2024.11.04.621686 (v2 2025-08). Related Peck et al. Nat Methods 2025 phantom-dataset paper (DOI 10.1038/s41592-025-02800-5) complements this. The portal itself has no single primary publication.

tools.name: ZeroCostDL4Mic
tools.approach: Notebook-based platform (originally Google Colab) that lets non-coding users train, fine-tune, and deploy U-Net, StarDist, YOLOv2, CARE, Noise2Void, Deep-STORM, fnet/pix2pix/CycleGAN and SAM models on their own data. DL4MicEverywhere (Hidalgo-Cenalmor et al., 2024 Nat Methods) packages this as portable containers for off-Colab use.
tools.architecture: Wrappers around canonical DL architectures
tools.training_data: User-supplied
tools.when_to_use: Lab-scale training of segmentation/denoising networks when no GPU cluster is available; first stop for users adopting DL in vEM/CLEM.
tools.limitations: Colab quotas/timeouts on free tier (mitigated by DL4MicEverywhere containers); not optimised for very large vEM volumes.
tools.compute: Colab GPU (free) or any container-capable host (DL4MicEverywhere).
tools.verification_notes: von Chamier L, Laine RF, Jukkala J et al. Nat Commun 12:2276 (2021). PMID 33859193. DL4MicEverywhere companion publication confirmed 2024.

tools.name: Ariadne / 3dEMtrace
tools.approach: Commercial / service-based ML segmentation of vEM datasets (neurons, glia, synapses, mitochondria, ER, Golgi); used as proofreading service for FlyWire connectome.
tools.architecture: Proprietary; presumed U-Net / FFN-style
tools.training_data: Customer + curated cellular EM datasets (proprietary)
tools.when_to_use: Outsourced large-scale connectomics segmentation/proofreading when no in-house pipeline available.
tools.limitations: Closed-source; pricing per project; no peer-reviewed methods paper at this writing.
tools.verification_notes: UNVERIFIED publication; mention only as service/tool. Chapter should not cite as a peer-reviewed method.

tools.name: Flood-Filling Networks (FFN)
tools.approach: Recurrent 3D CNN that iteratively extends a probability mask outward from a seed point until the object is fully captured; bypasses explicit boundary detection.
tools.architecture: Recurrent 3D CNN with object-mask iterative updates
tools.training_data: Songbird zebra finch SBEM + FlyEM datasets
tools.when_to_use: Highest-accuracy neuron segmentation at scale (used in Drosophila FAFB, hemibrain, MICrONS).
tools.limitations: Very compute-heavy; orders of magnitude slower than affinity+watershed pipelines; mostly Google-internal infrastructure.
tools.verification_notes: Nat. Methods 15:605-610; verified.

tools.name: Local Shape Descriptors (LSDs)
tools.approach: Auxiliary regression of local 10-D shape descriptors (statistics like diameter, elongation, direction within a sphere) alongside affinities; LSDs improve affinity-based pipelines to FFN-level accuracy at orders-of-magnitude less compute.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net predicting both affinities and LSDs jointly; downstream mutex watershed / hierarchical agglomeration
tools.training_data: CREMI Drosophila, FIB-25, FAFB, multiple datasets
tools.when_to_use: Production connectomics where FFN compute is prohibitive; benchmark accuracy ~ FFN at 100x less compute.
tools.limitations: Watershed merge errors at thin processes; needs careful post-processing for highest accuracy.
tools.compute: Single GPU per chunk; multi-node distributed for petabyte volumes
tools.verification_notes: Nat. Methods 20:295-303; verified.

tools.name: Mutex Watershed
tools.approach: Parameter-free graph partitioning that combines short-range attractive and long-range repulsive edges (from a deep network) into a single global segmentation; closely related to minimum spanning tree.
tools.architecture: Graph algorithm (deterministic, linearithmic)
tools.training_data: n/a
tools.when_to_use: When you have learned affinities (LSD pipeline) and want a deterministic, threshold-free partitioning.
tools.limitations: Quality limited by upstream affinity prediction.
tools.verification_notes: ECCV 2018; verified.

tools.name: PyTorch Connectomics (PyTC)
tools.approach: Open-source PyTorch framework for volumetric semantic/instance segmentation in connectomics; multi-task and semi-supervised training; supports synapse, mitochondria, nucleus, neuron segmentation.
tools.architecture: Configurable U-Net variants (2D/3D, residual, attention)
tools.training_data: CREMI (synapses), Lucchi (mitochondria), SNEMI3D, plus custom datasets
tools.when_to_use: When you want a customisable, well-documented PyTorch connectomics framework supporting various tasks (synapse, mitochondria, neuron).
tools.limitations: Preprint citation only (no journal publication); engineering quality high.
tools.compute: Single or multi-GPU; distributed via PyTorch DDP
tools.verification_notes: arXiv 2112.05754; verified preprint.

tools.name: Synaptic partner detection (Buhmann et al.)
tools.approach: CNN-based pipeline that predicts post-synaptic sites and their pre-synaptic partner vectors per voxel; trained from sparse point annotations. Simple post-processing yields directed synaptic-partner edges that can be combined with a neuron segmentation into a wiring diagram.
tools.architecture: U-Net with multi-task heads (postsynaptic mask + partner-offset field)
tools.training_data: Sparse human point annotations on the FAFB full adult fly brain ssTEM dataset.
tools.when_to_use: Connectomics pipelines requiring directed synaptic edges in fly/insect-scale datasets; baseline for synapse extraction in any pre-segmented neuron volume.
tools.limitations: Polyadic-synapse handling tuned to insects; vertebrate synapses with very different morphology need retraining; relies on a separate neuron segmentation for the wiring diagram.
tools.compute: Multi-GPU for whole-brain inference; CPU for postprocessing.
tools.verification_notes: Buhmann J, Sheridan A, Malin-Mayor C et al. Nat Methods 18:771-774 (2021). PMID 34168373, DOI 10.1038/s41592-021-01183-7.

tools.name: CDeep3M
tools.approach: Cloud-deployed Inception-ResNet-v2 + Caffe pipeline for 2D/3D segmentation of EM, X-ray, and LM data; preconfigured AMI on Amazon AWS.
tools.architecture: Inception-ResNet-V2 (2D/3D)
tools.training_data: User-supplied; benchmarked on EM and other modalities
tools.when_to_use: When local GPU infrastructure is unavailable and an AWS-deployable pipeline is needed.
tools.limitations: Caffe-era framework; some abandonment risk; cloud cost.
tools.verification_notes: Nat Methods 15:677-680; verified.

tools.name: CellMap / OpenOrganelle
tools.raw_name: CellMap / OpenOrganelle whole-cell organelle segmentation models
tools.approach: Suite of 3D U-Net (and U-Net variants) networks trained on Janelia's COSEM annotated FIB-SEM volumes, segmenting ~30-35 organelle and macromolecular classes (ER, mitochondria, Golgi, MVB, peroxisomes, ribosomes, microtubules, etc.) from 4 nm and 8 nm isotropic FIB-SEM data. Distributed through the OpenOrganelle portal alongside the reference data and the 2024-2025 CellMap Segmentation Challenge.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net (per-class or multi-class heads); separate models for 4 nm and 8 nm voxel sizes.
tools.training_data: OpenOrganelle (Heinrich et al. 2021): up to 35 organelle classes annotated across diverse FIB-SEM cell volumes; CellMap Challenge expansion (~289 volumes, ~40 classes) released 2024-2025.
tools.when_to_use: Whole-cell vEM organelle segmentation; first-choice baseline before re-training; benchmark for new vEM segmentation methods via the CellMap Challenge.
tools.limitations: Trained primarily on Janelia-style FIB-SEM at near-isotropic resolution; performance on SBEM, ssTEM or non-isotropic data is markedly worse and may need fine-tuning; class boundaries differ between models.
tools.compute: Multi-GPU inference for full cells; data IO frequently is the bottleneck.
tools.verification_notes: Heinrich L, Bennett D, Ackerman D et al. 'Whole-cell organelle segmentation in volume electron microscopy.' Nature 599:141-146 (2021). PMID 34616041, DOI 10.1038/s41586-021-03977-3. Models hosted at https://openorganelle.janelia.org/.

tools.name: MitoNet / Empanada
tools.approach: Generalist panoptic segmentation network for mitochondria across vEM modalities; trained on ~135k labelled mitochondria from 1.5M-image cellular EM corpus. Shipped via Empanada napari plugin.
tools.architecture: Panoptic 2D-stacked deep network (PanNetic; ResUNet-style encoder)
tools.training_data: ~135,000 mitochondrial instances curated from ~1.5e6 cellular EM images (CEM-MitoLab dataset)
tools.when_to_use: First-line mitochondria segmentation in vEM; out-of-the-box on diverse FIB-SEM/SBEM data.
tools.limitations: Mitochondria-only; for other organelles use Empanada fine-tuning workflow.
tools.verification_notes: Cell Systems 14(1):58-71; first author Conrad, corresponding Narayan.

tools.name: PlantSeg
tools.approach: 3D U-Net predicts cell boundary probabilities; graph partitioning (mutex watershed / multicut / GASP) recovers instance segmentation. Trained on plant tissue but generalises.
tools.architecture: 3D U-Net + graph partitioning
tools.training_data: Confocal / light-sheet plant tissues
tools.when_to_use: Tissue-level cell segmentation with thin boundaries; applicable to some FIB-SEM tissue data after retraining.
tools.limitations: Trained on plant data; transfer to animal cells requires fine-tuning.
tools.verification_notes: eLife 2020;9:e57613; verified.
